headline: Kolkata administration orders citywide safety checks after deadly hotel fire
summary: The Kolkata Municipal Corporation has ordered an indefinite closure of the Shikha Inn and a sweeping inspection of hotels and public spaces across the city following a fire that killed nine people.
details: A devastating fire at the Shikha Inn on Mirza Ghalib Street in Kolkata killed nine people, including several Bangladeshis. The tragedy has raised serious questions about regulatory oversight and safety measures at the hotel.

In response, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has ordered the indefinite closure of the hotel and announced a citywide safety inspection of hotels, commercial accommodations, markets, and other public gathering places.

Joint inspection committees will be formed for each of the city's 16 boroughs, starting August 25. These committees will examine fire safety arrangements and legal status, including whether establishments have the necessary licenses.

The KMC is also investigating its own monitoring system to determine where lapses occurred. Municipal Commissioner Smita Pandey stated that the building and licensing departments will be examined for any negligence.

Authorities have emphasized that hotel and business operators must comply with fire safety regulations and maintain adequate emergency and evacuation arrangements, as they cannot place the entire responsibility on government agencies.
caption:
A deadly hotel fire in Kolkata has triggered a citywide safety crackdown. Nine people lost their lives in the tragedy.

A devastating fire at the Shikha Inn on Mirza Ghalib Street in Kolkata killed nine people, including several Bangladeshis. The tragedy has raised serious questions about regulatory oversight and safety measures at the hotel.

In response, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has ordered the indefinite closure of the hotel and announced a citywide safety inspection of hotels, commercial accommodations, markets, and other public gathering places.

Joint inspection committees will be formed for each of the city's 16 boroughs, starting August 25. These committees will examine fire safety arrangements and legal status, including whether establishments have the necessary licenses.

The KMC is also investigating its own monitoring system to determine where lapses occurred. Municipal Commissioner Smita Pandey stated that the building and licensing departments will be examined for any negligence.

Authorities have emphasized that hotel and business operators must comply with fire safety regulations and maintain adequate emergency and evacuation arrangements, as they cannot place the entire responsibility on government agencies.

headline: Gas supply falls below 2,200 mmcfd as Moheshkhali LNG terminal runs out
summary: The Excelerate-operated FSRU stopped supplying the national grid today, leaving the country significantly below its daily demand of 3,800 mmcfd.
details: The Excelerate-operated LNG FSRU at Moheshkhali ran out of LNG and stopped supplying the national grid around 3pm today, according to Petrobangla officials.
With Summit's FSRU currently supplying around 550 mmcfd, the country's total gas supply has plummeted below 2,200 mmcfd against a national demand of approximately 3,800 mmcfd.
This disruption follows a period of instability for the terminal, which had previously shut down due to a fire on July 21 and subsequent technical issues.
The terminal, which can supply up to 600 mmcfd, has now completely exhausted its LNG inventory.
Bangladesh is now largely dependent on Summit's terminal for imported LNG until a new cargo arrives.
According to the government's procurement plan, the terminal is unlikely to resume operations until the next consignment arrives on August 23.
caption:
Bangladesh's gas supply has plummeted below 2,200 mmcfd, far short of the 3,800 mmcfd daily demand.

The Excelerate-operated LNG FSRU at Moheshkhali ran out of LNG and stopped supplying the national grid around 3pm today, according to Petrobangla officials.

With Summit's FSRU currently supplying around 550 mmcfd, the country's total gas supply has plummeted below 2,200 mmcfd against a national demand of approximately 3,800 mmcfd.

This disruption follows a period of instability for the terminal, which had previously shut down due to a fire on July 21 and subsequent technical issues.

The terminal, which can supply up to 600 mmcfd, has now completely exhausted its LNG inventory.

Bangladesh is now largely dependent on Summit's terminal for imported LNG until a new cargo arrives.

According to the government's procurement plan, the terminal is unlikely to resume operations until the next consignment arrives on August 23.
